clue.text: See 6
Charges published on hospital's downward course

parts.note: dues are fees or charges paid
a book that is out has been published
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Fees announced for a hospital are going steadily downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: On a conventional map south is at the bottom, so heading that way is a downward bearing.

clue.text: Drop reform of vehicles? Losing intensive care just the start

indicators.note: reforming a word reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged
losing means some letters are taken away from the word
only the opening letter of each of the two words is used

explanation.surface: A policy to abandon transport reform, with only intensive care left at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' takes I and C (the starts of 'intensive care') out of VEHICLES, and 'reform of' rearranges the remaining VEHLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan is to postpone or abandon it, put it aside on a shelf.

clue.text: Way to cook potatoes required game inside

indicators.note: inside means the game is placed within the other word

parts.note: something due is owed or required
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A recipe says potatoes must be cooked with game meat inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like meat for the pot; it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse potatoes are a classic French preparation: mashed, piped into rosettes and baked.

clue.text: Having done time, gaoled anew

indicators.note: made anew means rebuilt from scratch, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner who has served a sentence is locked up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having done time' suggests a prison term; here it means having lasted a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient has existed for ages, so it has endured a great stretch of time.

clue.text: Take place of doctor to cure me

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient asks to take over from the doctor and heal themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take place' looks like 'replace', but here it means to happen; 'doctor' is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A prediction or wish that is fulfilled is said to happen, or materialise, in reality.

clue.text: Medic is compelled into humanitarian crisis

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
one who ought to do something is obliged or compelled to

explanation.surface: A doctor feels obliged to go into a disaster zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lack of rain causes famine, a common cause of humanitarian emergencies.

clue.text: Compulsion at the heart of junior doctor

indicators.note: at the heart of means placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a son is a junior member of the family
an urge is a compulsion

explanation.surface: A compulsion lies at the core of a young hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical practitioner who operates is one kind of physician.

clue.text: Medical instrument for removal of fungus

indicators.note: removal of means the word that follows is taken out

parts.note: forceps are tongs used by surgeons
the word 'for' itself is what is taken out

explanation.surface: A doctor names the tool used to cut away a fungal growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but is the very letters removed from the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceps are edible wild mushrooms, the porcini of Italian cooking, so a kind of fungus.

clue.text: MOs to heal sick and sickening

indicators.note: sick letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Doctors are there to heal the ill and the nauseous.
explanation.walkthrough: MOs are medical officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revolting or repugnant makes one feel sick, so it is sickening.

clue.text: Mae West broadcast? Boatman is on time in New York

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the sailor sits above the time

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
Jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor
ET is Eastern Time, the zone New York keeps

explanation.surface: The setter, appearing on New York time, broadcasts about the film star Mae West.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's own name, read here as a sailor. A Mae West is wartime slang for an inflatable life jacket, from the actress's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen called their inflatable life vests after the buxom actress, so the name is a nickname for one.

clue.text: Severe laceration seen in hospital department

indicators.note: seen in means the cut is found inside the department

parts.note: A and E (accident and emergency) is the British emergency department
a cut is a laceration

explanation.surface: A bad gash is treated in casualty.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute pain or shortage is intense and serious, so severe.

clue.text: Doctor to find cure later

indicators.note: curing something processes and changes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician will come up with a remedy at some later time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the medic but is the verb meaning to tamper with; 'cure' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to tamper with them, changing them from what they were.

clue.text: American version of Doctor in the House?

definitions.text: American version of Doctor in the House?

parts.words: American version of Doctor in the House?
parts.note: a hospital doctor in training in the US, who once literally lived in the hospital, is so called; Doctor in the House is a British comedy about junior doctors

explanation.surface: Asks what the US remake of the British medical comedy Doctor in the House would be.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor in the House is a British film and TV comedy about junior hospital doctors; the US term for such a doctor also suggests someone living in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: In American hospitals a physician in specialist training is so named, and the word also means one who lives at a place.

clue.text: Plastic surgeon needs letters to go out with hospital worker?

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters are reshaped
out means these letters leave the word

parts.note: the letters to remove are those spelling 'go'

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon must go out with a hospital colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic surgeon' looks like one job; 'Plastic' is the anagram signal for SURNE, what is left once G and O go 'out' of SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward carer who tends patients is a typical hospital employee; the query marks that the definition is an example.

clue.text: Pointless change causes irritation

indicators.note: the compass points S and W are removed

parts.note: to switch is to change

explanation.surface: A futile alteration only annoys people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' looks like 'futile' but means losing compass points: S and W (south, west).
explanation.definitionFit: An irritation of the skin is a tickling urge to scratch.

clue.text: Put pressure on doctor

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to lace a drink is to doctor it with something

explanation.surface: An instruction to lean on a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is the verb to spike, as when lacing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To set or position something somewhere is to put it there.

clue.text: Poetical colour of beautiful boat in seascape, agree narrators

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Storytellers agree on the colour of a lovely boat in a sea painting.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-Cat they 'went to sea in a beautiful pea-green boat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's nonsense poem gives its famous boat this pale yellowish-green shade.

clue.text: Report of added numbers leading to deaths

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so this signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: added means more, extra; a tally is a count of numbers

explanation.surface: An account of rising figures resulting in fatalities.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal wound kills, and an adverb meaning fatally describes harm ending in death.

clue.text: Doctor gets the girls — that's sweet

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A doctor is joined by the girls, which is nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's sweet' looks like a comment on the scene; it defines a sugary syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark syrup, a by-product of refining sugar, is a sweet substance.

clue.text: Clue for part of hospital with a problem

parts.note: a part of a hospital is a ward; the answer read as an instruction, draw written back to front, spells that room

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hint about a troublesome hospital section.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as wordplay gives WARD, a part of a hospital, so it is a fitting clue for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or snag is a problem with something.

clue.text: Evil or sick? It's all the same, if you're young

definitions.text: sick? It's all the same, if you're young
definitions.meaning: in young people's slang 'sick' means excellent, and so does this word

explanation.surface: Bad or ill? Young people don't see the difference.
explanation.walkthrough: In youth slang both 'sick' and this word mean brilliant, so to the young they are the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sinful in standard use and great in slang, matching each definition.

clue.text: Drop medical vehicle's display

indicators.note: the words put this answer on display within their letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop the ambulance show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' means to give birth, as a cow drops a calf.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock farmers say a cow drops a calf when it gives birth to one.

clue.text: Treatment: to swallow radium (it's poisonous)

indicators.note: swallowing means the radium symbol goes inside

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment
Ra is the chemical symbol for radium

explanation.surface: A therapy involving swallowing radioactive radium is toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American arrow poison paralyses muscles, a toxin.

clue.text: Cosmetic specialist and doctor are in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disordered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beautician and a physician have both landed in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cosmetic specialist' suggests make-up; it is someone who improves only the surface of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and paperhanger specialises in cosmetic improvements to rooms.

clue.text: Definitely uninteresting, lacking lustre on top

definitions.text: Definitely uninteresting, lacking lustre on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the tops of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Something certainly boring and lacking any shine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and the first letters of its first four words spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boring and without shine is lacklustre in both senses.

clue.text: It's used to clean edges of surgeon's instrument — Boatman closes it

indicators.note: closes it means the sailor comes at the end
only the outside letters of the instrument are kept

parts.note: a surgeon's saw is a bone-cutting tool
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: An item for cleaning the rim of a surgical tool, with the setter finishing the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's name, read as a sailor; the edges of SAW are S and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of absorbent material on a stick is used to clean wounds or decks.

clue.text: See 17 across
One might call doctor for blood type before injecting drug into sick person

indicators.note: before means the blood group comes first

parts.note: B is a blood group

indicators.note: injecting means the drug is put inside the sick person

parts.note: a leper suffers from leprosy
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor is summoned over a blood test before drugs are given to a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager that beeps is used to summon a hospital doctor.

clue.text: Hospital worker is disciplined

definitions.meaning: an attendant who does non-medical jobs in a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital porter behaves well.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a hospital attendant and an adjective for neat and methodical.
